subject: MedAlign: post-call recap — isolation & network acceptance path
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@medalign.com>
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@medalign.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MedAlign: post-call recap — isolation & network acceptance path

Hi Alice / Marcus — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed or mis-characterized.

Top pain & drivers you shared
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI on-prem or in a customer-controlled VPC within their cloud tenancy for the inference layer (no model-hosted egress).
- Appliance must be air-gapped or quasi-airgapped: no outbound internet from the inference hosts; all updates and telemetry must be routed via approved proxy/bastion.
- Strong need for KMS/HSM integration (FIPS 140-2 compatible) and customer-managed key lifecycle.
- SOC 2 evidence and a short audit window (30–45 days) for initial procurement.

Technical constraints we captured
- No direct outbound to public model registries from GPU subnet; model artifacts will be staged into a private S3 bucket in your account and pulled via internal pipelines.
- Network egress must be through an approved NAT/proxy with static IPs (will provide IP range expectations).
- Inference hosts cannot initiate any calls to third-party telemetry endpoints; only allowed connections are to the internal artifact store, KMS endpoint, and your observability collectors.

What Redwood can do (high level)
- Private deployment package: control plane in your VPC, inference runtime inside your tenancy (we support AWS, GCP VPC peering, and on-prem with equivalent constraints).
- Support for customer KMS/HSM and optional HSM-backed key wrapping for model and cache encryption.
- We can provide SOC 2 extracts and a short compliance pack (see attached SOC2-extract.pdf).

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Technical deep dive (90 min) — proposed week of 6/1. Ben to lead — we’ll bring network diagrams and example IAM roles.
2) Provide network acceptance criteria doc and IP ranges — Redwood will deliver a first draft by 5/26 (attachment: network-diagram.pdf stub).
3) Procurement checklist for your SOW — Marissa to coordinate commercial and contracting questions.

Action owners & timeline
- Ben Carter (redwood) — tech deep dive & network acceptance doc (deliver by 2026-05-26).
- Marissa Cole (redwood) — procurement checklist and initial SOW draft (deliver by 2026-06-04).
- Alice / Marcus (MedAlign) — confirm acceptable deep-dive slots and upload network topology + KMS endpoint URIs.

Open questions we need answered before the deep dive
- Ability to stage model artifacts in a private bucket in your tenancy (yes/no)?
- KMS/HSM vendor and whether we can test key wrapping in a sandbox prior to production.
- Any fixed maintenance blackout windows for the GPU nodes?

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf (stub), SOC2-extract.pdf (stub)

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@medalign.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@medalign.com>, procurement@medalign.com
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedAlign: post-call recap — isolation & network acceptance path

Hi Neha — thanks for the clear summary. This looks right to me; a couple of clarifications and questions below.

Clarifications
- We are targeting keeping inference within our AWS account for patient data (us-west-2). Model artifacts can be staged in a private S3 bucket, yes — as long as the bucket policy restricts access to roles from our account.
- KMS vendor is AWS KMS with CloudHSM; we require HSM-backed key material for production keys.

Questions
1) For the SOC2 materials: can you provide the scope pages that specifically call out data handling for hosted vs private deployments? Our audit team will need that.
2) On the no-outbound rule: would it be possible to allow outbound to Redwood-owned update endpoints through a customer-controlled proxy if we vet them? Or do you require a pull model where we pull signed artifacts from your release bucket?
3) For the deep dive, we prefer Tue 6/2 or Wed 6/3 in the morning Pacific.

Marcus will upload a high-level network diagram and a short checklist of internal IP ranges by EOD Monday. Procurement is on copy — they will follow up separately on the SOW cadence.

Best,
Alice

--
Alice Wong
VP of Engineering, MedAlign Health
alice.wong@medalign.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@medalign.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@medalign.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedAlign: post-call recap — isolation & network acceptance path

Thanks Neha / Alice — quick technical notes ahead of the deep dive. I'm attaching a compact network diagram and a sample acceptance checklist (see network-diagram.pdf). High level answers below and proposed defaults we can negotiate during the call: 

1) Artifact delivery model- Preferred: customer-managed S3 (you stage, we pull via signed role). This matches your constraint and means no outbound egress from GPU hosts to public internet. Alternative (if you prefer): we push signed, time-limited artifacts into your bucket via cross-account role, still no public egress required.

2) Proxy / egress model- We support both pull and proxy approaches. If you allow our update endpoints through a vetted proxy with static IPs, we can reduce operational friction (push updates, health checks). If not, pull-only is fully supported. Either way, the runtime will not accept connections to public telemetry.

3) KMS/HSM integration- We can use CloudHSM-backed keys via AWS KMS. For the initial PoC we can use envelope encryption with a test key; production must use HSM-backed keys and we'll run a brief key-wrapping smoke test with your security team.

4) Observability & telemetry- By default telemetry is disabled on private deployments. We will enable only the collectors you list; any other outbound is blocked at the host firewall.

Proposed deliverable for 5/26 (what I'll send):
- Network acceptance checklist with example iptables rules and allowed ports.
- Example IAM role policies for model artifact access.
- Minimal runbook for sandbox key-wrapping test.

Forwarded attachment: network-diagram.pdf (stub)

Looking forward to 6/2 morning (I prefer 9–11am PT). I can carve out an hour if you want to go deeper on the runtime constraints.

Thanks — Ben
